response.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT link_to_major, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM member WHERE link_to_major IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(link_to_major) <> '' GROUP BY link_to_major), shares AS (SELECT link_to_major, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM grouped) AS share FROM grouped), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share FROM shares s, avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_members, AVG(share) AS avg_share_of_above, AVG(share - (SELECT avg_share FROM avg_share)) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: A member's major is 'missing' when link_to_major is NULL or an empty/whitespace-only string; both are excluded before grouping. The request does not say which form of missing it means.
The total count is the sum of member counts over the retained groups, and each group's share is its count divided by that total. Shares are computed with REAL division so they are not truncated.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-group shares. Each group counts once regardless of its size.
Groups are keyed only by link_to_major as stored. The major table is not joined, so a major ID with no matching major row still forms its own group.
The average excess is the mean over the above-average groups of (share minus average share). It is not the excess of the mean share over the average.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat only NULL as a missing major; empty-string majors form their own group.
